ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides whether the fix subagent is resumed or fresh, and how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/re-review-prompt.md` to fill in the scoped re-review template.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on `haiku`, resumed or fresh as fix-loop.md says. Its job is to change `--dry_run` to `--dry-run` at `docs/sync.md:12` and commit. The prompt carries F1 word for word and the Task 3 brief, with no other context.

ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package .sdd/14-buoy-sync/... PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD` for the fix commit only. BASE is the Task 3 head, and HEAD is the fix commit. This writes the diff file for the re-review.

ACTION: Dispatch the scoped re-review on `sonnet` with the re-review template. It gets F1 and the diff file path that the script reports. It does not get a pre-rated severity or a "do not flag" list.

ACTION: If the re-review reports F1 ADDRESSED with no new Critical or Important finding, append `Task 3: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)` to `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/progress.md`, then dispatch Task 4.

Task 3 has one open Important finding, F1. `docs/sync.md:12` says `--dry_run`, but the code, the help text and the tests all use `--dry-run`. A reader who copies the documented flag gets an error. I am sending the one-word fix to a subagent, then a scoped re-review. Task 3 stays open until that review is clean.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The mismatch cannot show up in a test run. No code or test reads `docs/sync.md`, so only a reviewer reading the diff could catch it.
- The review rule treats Important findings as blocking whatever their size. A one-character docs fix still goes through fix and re-review.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
